summary.name: SREcon16 Performance Checklists for SREs
summary.one_liner: A 2016 blog post by Brendan Gregg summarizing his SREcon16 closing talk on performance checklists for site reliability engineers, including several Linux troubleshooting checklists.
use_cases: Troubleshooting Linux performance issues during an incident
Building custom monitoring dashboards for SRE on-call
Checking disk I/O problems on Linux servers
Diagnosing network and TCP retransmit issues on Linux
Narrowing down CPU bottlenecks with standard Linux tools
summary.what_it_does: The page is a blog post summarizing a talk on performance checklists for SRE incident response, written by Brendan Gregg, a Senior Performance Architect at Netflix. It lists Linux checklists for overall performance (uptime, vmstat, mpstat, pidstat, iostat, free, sar, top), disk I/O, networking, and CPU, each as an ordered series of commands and what to check with each. It notes the checklists are meant to be implemented as GUI dashboards and that some items rely on bcc/BPF tools (such as ext4slower, biolatency, tcpretrans). It also mentions Netflix-specific triage checklists that are not reproduced in the post, and points to slides and video of the talk.
notable: Linux Perf Analysis in 60s checklist of ten commands for fast triage
Disk, network, and CPU checklists ordered for incident response
Relies on bcc/BPF tracing tools for several items
Written from Netflix SRE incident response perspective
caveats: Only Linux checklists are reproduced here; the other eight checklists are in the slides, not the post
Some checks depend on bcc/BPF tools or optional hardware tools (smartctl, ioerr_cnt) being available
Netflix-specific checklists are described but not included
